subject: Pilot metrics workbook and acceptance criteria
messages:

Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot metrics workbook and acceptance criteria

Hi Samantha —

Great to see the pilot moving forward. Attached is an initial MAP worksheet focused on the performance evaluation we discussed: 'quantum_map_v1.xlsx'. The benchmarking tab outlines the scoped scenarios, test harness configuration, and success criteria. Key items called out in short:

- Workload definitions:
  - Short prompts (<=64 tokens), medium prompts (65–256 tokens), long prompts (>256 tokens)
  - Mixed request mix: 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long (by request count)
  - Representative concurrency patterns: ramp tests (1→8), sustained runs at target concurrency, and burst profiles

- Metrics to capture:
  - Latency: P50 / P95 / P99 per prompt class (tail behavior is critical)
  - Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec sustained for each concurrency level
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token): median and cold start percentiles (measure both warm cache and cold VM starts)
  - Concurrency saturation points (at what concurrency do we see queueing/backpressure)
  - Quality checks: sample outputs evaluated against your evaluation rubric (top-level pass/fail for regressions)

- Success criteria (proposal):
  - P95 latency for short prompts < 150ms, for medium prompts < 300ms
  - TTFT median < 200ms (warm); cold-start TTFT < 400ms
  - Sustained throughput >= 50 req/s for the mixed workload at concurrency 6
  - No more than 1% requests with server-side errors during a 30-minute sustained run

We recommend Redwood run the initial benchmark in our Dedicated staging pool and share raw CSVs and a summarized pilot_summary.pdf so your engineering team can validate. Proposed timeline:
  - Run initial scoped bench: Sep 6–8
  - Review results and iterate: Sep 9–11
  - Finalize acceptance and move to canary: Sep 13

Questions for you: would you like cold VM restarts included by default, and do you want encryption/KMS-specific measurements in the acceptance criteria?

Thanks — attaching the workbook now.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Diego —

Thanks for the detailed workbook. A few clarifications before we lock the MAP: 

- Please include explicit cold-start measurements (cold VM + cold KV cache) as part of the TTFT targets; we need to understand worst-case latency for on‑demand usage.
- Can you add a short end‑to‑end user perceived latency metric (from our app gateway through to token stream start)? That will help correlate infra numbers to product UX.
- We need to see KMS key-handling latency added as a controlled variable for throughput tests (we use an HSM-backed KMS).

Also adding procurement on the thread — they'll need the draft SOW and an expected licence/usage estimate to start internal approval.

Subject: Re: Pilot metrics workbook and acceptance criteria — preliminary results

Diego / team —

Attached are the raw CSVs and a short summary: 'benchmark_run_results.csv'. Highlights from the Sep 6–8 runs: 

- Warm steady-state (concurrency 6, mixed workload):
  - P50 latency (short prompts): 34 ms
  - P95 latency (short prompts): 118 ms
  - P95 latency (medium prompts): 255 ms
  - Sustained throughput: ~60 req/s (tokens/sec equivalent ~2300 tokens/s)
  - TTFT (median, warm): 82 ms
  - Server errors: 0.2% (network retries; no modelOOM)

- Cold-profile (fresh VMs, cold KV cache):
  - TTFT median (cold): 312 ms
  - Cold P95: 485 ms
  - Observed tail occasionally spikes when node provisioning overlapped with load; recommend isolating cold-start measurement windows

- Concurrency stress (ramp to 12):
  - System holds up to concurrency 8 with modest latency increases; beyond 8 we observed queueing and P95 growth (short prompts P95 jumped to ~620 ms at concurrency 12)
  - CPU utilization and host-level queues indicate saturation on the model-serving threads beyond target concurrency

- KMS simulation (HSM-mode added by Karthik):
  - Added ~8–12 ms extra per request in observed path; throughput impact marginal for warm runs but noticeable for short prompt TTFT in cold scenarios

Notes and recommendations:
- Proposed acceptance tweaks: make short-prompt P95 target <= 120ms (aligned with measured 118ms) and TTFT warm median <= 100ms; keep cold TTFT target <= 400ms.
- For production canary, recommend starting with concurrency cap 6 and autoscale trigger at 75% CPU to avoid tail spikes.
- Provide the Quantum team the raw CSVs and a condensed pilot_summary.pdf; I'll produce both by end of day Sep 9.

Attachments: benchmark_run_results.csv

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot metrics workbook and acceptance criteria — pilot summary and next steps

Samantha / Rajiv —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is the pilot_summary.pdf that pulls the key tables and a short canary plan. TL;DR from our runs: the workload and instrumentation you requested produced strong warm-state performance and clear cold-start characteristics. Key points: 

- Final suggested acceptance criteria (proposed):
  - Short prompts P95 <= 120 ms
  - Medium prompts P95 <= 300 ms
  - Warm TTFT median <= 100 ms; cold TTFT median <= 400 ms
  - Sustained throughput >= 50 req/s for mixed workload at concurrency 6
  - Errors <= 1% during a 30-minute sustained run

- Observed gating conditions:
  - Concurrency > 8 causes tail risk; recommend canary concurrency cap at 6 and step to 8 after monitoring 48h
  - KMS/HSM adds ~10ms; we accounted for that in TTFT targets

Next steps:
  1) Procurement: Vanessa and I will send the SOW/usage estimate and a proposed canary schedule (targeting Sep 15–17 for canary)
  2) Quantum: please confirm acceptance of the proposed criteria and whether you want us to run an extra cold-only test window prior to canary
  3) Ops/Engineering: Marissa — final CSVs and pilot_summary.pdf attached; Karthik — note included re: KMS instrumentation

If you approve, we'll prepare the SOW and schedule the DocuSign link.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
